page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, this instance maintains a balanced resource distribution of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include integrated local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options for persistent disk requirements.

From a resource density perspective, the n4d-standard-48 offers a predictable cost-to-performance ratio for workloads requiring substantial parallel processing without the overhead of specialized hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance, avoiding the resource contention typical of shared-core or burstable configurations. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and public IPv4 addresses requires users to factor in external network and storage attachments when planning deployments.

This instance configuration is suited for multi-threaded applications, enterprise web serving, application servers, and moderate database workloads. The 48-core capacity supports concurrent task execution, making it appropriate for continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, container orchestration nodes, and general-purpose backend processing.
